TransformersTransformer: a neural architecture built entirely on attention mechanisms.
Credits: The Illustrated Transformer –Jay Alammar
Transformer ArchitectureCore Components Encoder Stack:produces contextual representations of the input.Decoder Stack: usesthe encoder's output and previous decoder outputs to generate the target sequence.Self-Attention Mechanism: allowsthe model to focus on different parts of the input sequence when processing each token.Feed-Forward Neural Networks: apply nonlinear transformation per token.Key idea: no recurrence, no convolution —only attention.
Why Self-Attention Replaced RNNsIn RNNs: –Information between distant tokens flows through O(n) steps –Computation is sequential, i.e.hard to parallelizeIn Transformers: –Self-attention allows each token to directly attend to all other tokens in the sequence, producing contextualised representations–Computation within each layer is parallelizable across sequence positionsTrade-off: –Attention time and memory scale quadraticallywith sequence length 𝑂(𝑛2)

Prior BERT : ELMoELMo(Peters et al., 2018; NAACL 2018 best paper)–Train two separate unidirectional LMs (left-to-right and right-to-left) based on LSTMs–Feature-based approach: pre-trained representations used as input to task-specific models–Trained on single sentences from 1B word benchmark (Chelbaet al., 2014)
Train separate left-to-right and right-to-left LMs Apply as “Pre-trained Embeddings”
BERT : Key ContributionsA deep Transformer encoder model pre-trained on large corporaThe key: learning representations based on bidirectional contextWhy? Because both left and right contexts are important to understand the meaning of words.Example #1: we went to the river bank.Example #2: I need to go to bankto make a deposit.Pre-training objectives: (1) masked language modeling + (2) next sentence prediction,State-of-the-art performance (2018) on a large set of sentence-level and token-level tasks.
Masked Language Modelling (MLM)All input tokens participate in bidirectional self-attention BUT only the 15% of tokens sampled for prediction contribute to the training loss.Average cross-entropy loss over these selected positions
Network weights are updated based on average CE loss over the sampled tokens

Instruction tuning
The Dominant Architecture of Transformer-based 
LLMs
 GPT-3:
– Decoder-only Transformer
– Causal attention
– LayerNorm, residual blocks, etc.
 Modern LLMs (LLaMA, Mistral, DeepSeek, etc.):
– Same core architecture
– Sometimes improved normalization or efficiency
– Minor architectural refinements
– But the core is the same.
Foundation vs Instruction Tuned Models
Foundation
● Coherent, fluent generation
● Completion and continuation
● Vast world knowledge
● Potentially harmful outputs
● Difficult to control
● Misaligned with our values
Instruction Tuned
● Foundation ability and more
● Controllable by prompt
● Less need to fine-tune
● Follows any command 
● Slight hit to performance
● Sensitive to prompt template
Summary 
 Pretraining
– Large-scale self-supervised learning
– Autoregressive next-token prediction
– Trained on massive text corpora
 What It Produces
– Fluent text
– World knowledge correlations
– In-context learning capability
– Generative foundation model
 What It does NOT Guarantee
– Instruction following
– Helpfulness or safety
– Truthfulness

Pretraining Large Language Models
Jingyuan Sun
Lecturer of Natural Language Processing

Learning Outcomes
Define LLM pretraining and explain why it is self-supervised.
Compare Transformer variants (encoder-only, encoder–decoder, decoder-
only) and explain why modern LLMs use decoder-only with causal 
attention.
Formulate the training objective: autoregressive probability factorisation, 
cross-entropy loss, and the difference between training vs inference.
Evaluate implications: limitations (e.g., hallucinations/bias), the impact of 
scale/compute, and how pretraining connects to adaptation and instruction 
tuning.
